claims.quote: At the end of each year, the books of every nation are examined. If France is found in our debt, probably we are in the debt of some nation which owes France, and so on with all the nations.
claims.description: An international council audits and clears trade balances among nations through a multilateral accounting system.

claims.quote: the international council inspects the commodities interchanged by the nations, to see that they are of perfect quality.
claims.description: An international council inspects goods traded between nations for quality to preserve amity.

claims.quote: In national staples; a basis of agreement as to what staples shall be accepted, and in what proportions, for settlement of accounts, being a preliminary to trade relations.
claims.description: International trade balances are settled in agreed-upon national staple commodities rather than money.

claims.quote: if a man at twenty-one emigrates from England to America, England loses all the expense of his maintenance and education, and America gets a workman for nothing. America accordingly makes England an allowance.
claims.description: Nations pay each other indemnities for emigrants, compensating the country that raised and educated them.

claims.quote: An American credit card is just as good in Europe as American gold used to be, and on precisely the same condition, namely, that it be exchanged into the currency of the country you are traveling in.
claims.description: Government-issued credit cards replace money and can be exchanged for foreign credit cards abroad, with the amount charged between nations.

claims.quote: Not only is our cooking done at the public kitchens, as I told you last night, but the service and quality of the meals are much more satisfactory if taken at the dining-house.
claims.description: Cooking is done in public kitchens and most people dine in ward public dining-houses rather than at home.

claims.quote: a continuous waterproof covering had been let down so as to inclose the sidewalk and turn it into a well lighted and perfectly dry corridor
claims.description: City sidewalks are covered by retractable waterproof canopies that protect pedestrians from rain.

claims.quote: in the twentieth century they put up one umbrella over all the heads.
claims.description: Collective public infrastructure replaces individual umbrellas, symbolizing a shift from individualism to concerted social organization.

claims.quote: If we expect to dine here, we put in our orders the night before, selecting anything in market, according to the daily reports in the papers.
claims.description: Meals are pre-ordered from public dining-houses based on daily market reports in the newspapers.

claims.quote: The waiters are young men in the unclassified grade of the industrial army who are assignable to all sorts of miscellaneous occupations not requiring special skill.
claims.description: All citizens serve in a national industrial army, with young recruits assigned to jobs such as waiting tables.

claims.quote: Equal wealth and equal opportunities of culture which all persons now enjoy have simply made us all members of one class
claims.description: Equality of wealth and education abolishes class distinctions and the stigma of menial service.

claims.quote: All the industrial and professional guilds have clubhouses as extensive as this, as well as country, mountain, and seaside houses for sport and rest in vacations.
claims.description: Guilds maintain grand clubhouses and vacation houses, with luxurious public life and simple private homes.

claims.quote: There ensued an era of mechanical invention, scientific discovery, art, musical and literary productiveness to which no previous age of the world offers anything comparable.
claims.description: The transition to a cooperative economic order triggers an unprecedented flowering of invention, science, and the arts.
claims.stated_time: early part of the twentieth century

claims.quote: The printing department has no censorial powers. It is bound to print all that is offered it, but prints it only on condition that the author defray the first cost out of his credit.
claims.description: The national printing department publishes any author's book at the author's expense from his credit, with no censorship.

claims.quote: The author fixes this royalty at any figure he pleases. Of course if he puts it unreasonably high it is his own loss, for the book will not sell.
claims.description: Authors earn royalties credited as time exempt from national service, letting successful writers write full time.

claims.quote: They vote upon the acceptance of statues and paintings for the public buildings, and their favorable verdict carries with it the artist's remission from other tasks to devote himself to his vocation.
claims.description: The public votes on art for public buildings and successful artists are released from other service.

claims.quote: The highest of all honors in the nation, higher than the presidency, which calls merely for good sense and devotion to duty, is the red ribbon awarded by the vote of the people to the great authors, artists, engineers, physicians, and inventors of the generation.
claims.description: A popularly voted red ribbon is the nation's highest honor, awarded to great authors, artists, engineers, physicians and inventors.

claims.quote: The people who take the paper pay the expense of its publication, choose its editor, and remove him when unsatisfactory.
claims.description: Newspapers are funded by subscribers through credits, who elect and remove editors, with the nation acting only as publisher.

claims.quote: The subscribers to the paper now elect somebody as editor, who, if he accepts the office, is discharged from other service during his incumbency.
claims.description: Elected newspaper editors are released from national service and subscribers indemnify the nation for their support.
